message.grandwitch.offer: <%s> Here, dear, try the little cake I have just baked.
message.grandwitch.mouse:
You eat it... you shrink... squeak! You are a mouse.
You can squeeze through gaps half a block high; crouch and use a chest to nibble the food in it; you can dig soft ground into a tunnel and hide in it.
A mouse squeaks now and then, and every cat within 32 blocks turns to it; keep crouching and it keeps quiet.
command.grandwitch.came: The Grand Witch has come, at %s
command.grandwitch.no_room: There is nowhere to stand near here
message.grandwitch.call: <%s> Come here, dear... I have something nice for you. Right-click me.
message.grandwitch.enough: <%s> You have one already, dear. Eat, eat.
message.grandwitch.squeak_heard: Squeak! %s cats are coming for you
message.grandwitch.child_turned: The Grand Witch has turned a child into a mouse!
item.grandwitch.antidote.tip:
Drink it and a mouse is a person again. Or give it to another mouse (right-click), a child too.
A golden carrot, a spider eye and a glass bottle: one in the inventory grid; thrown into a cauldron with water over a fire, two.
command.grandwitch.no_hut: It cannot be built here: it needs 7 x 7 clear ground
message.grandwitch.alarm: The village bells are ringing! The Grand Witch has shown herself, and she is shining.
message.grandwitch.trespass: A shriek from the house: the Grand Witch is coming back!
message.grandwitch.dig_level: You can only dig soft ground level with your feet, not up or down
book.grandwitch.diary.1:
Another village.

There are children all over the place, and they give me a headache. I hate children: their laughter, the smell of milk on them.

But they are the easiest to coax: a basket of cakes, a few soft words, and they follow me like lambs.
book.grandwitch.diary.2:
Today I was a little girl with a basket, in a red hood, and the villagers all said how sweet I was. Ha.

Tomorrow it may be a lass in an apron with plaits, or an old woman on a stick, or a trader on the road, or a nanny minding other people's children. No one will look at me twice.
book.grandwitch.diary.3:
My cakes are marvellous.

They look like anything out of the oven, and when someone bites one, even I cannot say whether it is for good or ill: that depends on my mood at the time.

Some laugh with delight. Some squeak. I do love to watch.
book.grandwitch.diary.4:
The cats and dogs of the village are infuriating. I have hardly come near when they bristle at me and growl in their throats.

And those iron lumps: when I show what I am, they beat me till my head rings.

And that wretched bell, which rings the moment I show myself, so that I shine for all to see.
book.grandwitch.diary.5:
What I hate most is mice!

The sight of one of those squeaking things and I am in a rage, and must run it down and stamp on it. But when they get into a hole I cannot see them, and no cat can follow, and it drives me mad.

And the ones I make myself are just the same.
book.grandwitch.diary.6:
My potions: one bottle, and grown or small, they shrink to mice.

But once a fool held a wooden shield up in front of him, and the whole bottle broke on it, and my fine work was wasted.

I shall not let them be so pleased with themselves again.
book.grandwitch.diary.7:
I must keep something by me for myself, in case some day I drink the wrong thing.

A golden carrot, a spider eye, an empty bottle, thrown together into a cauldron over a fire, and boiled till it bubbles: it makes two. There are other ways, but they make less, and are slow.
book.grandwitch.diary.8:
My little house.

If anyone dares to come in, I can hear it however far I am, and be back in a twinkling, and they will see what I can do.

If I should die some day, everyone I changed will be changed back. I cannot bear the thought.
message.grandwitch.reward.apple: There was a golden apple hidden in the cake!
message.grandwitch.reward.emeralds: Some emeralds fall out of the cake!
message.grandwitch.reward.heal: A warmth runs through you, and you feel splendid.
message.grandwitch.reward.speed: There is a wind at your heels.
message.grandwitch.reward.luck: You feel as if today is your lucky day.
message.grandwitch.antidote_unneeded: You have no need of it now
message.grandwitch.call.potion: <%s> Fine potions, %s emeralds a bottle: come to me with emeralds in your hand, and use me.
message.grandwitch.call.curse: <%s> A good thing for you, for nothing: use me.
message.grandwitch.potion.ask: <%s> %s emeralds a bottle: come to me with the emeralds in your hand.
message.grandwitch.potion.sold: <%s> A fine potion: you will feel the better for it.
message.grandwitch.curse.gift: <%s> Take it, you will find a use for it.
message.grandwitch.curse.enough: <%s> I have given you one already. Do not be greedy.
message.grandwitch.curse.warm: Something in your pocket seems warm...
message.grandwitch.curse.hot: Something in your pocket is getting hotter!
item.grandwitch.curse_lore: It is warm to the touch...
message.grandwitch.nanny.calls: <%s> Come along, children, come with me: I will take you somewhere nice.
message.grandwitch.nanny.chat: <%s> Hush, I have the children to see to.
book.grandwitch.diary.9:
I have several faces.

Sometimes I give cakes. Sometimes I sell potions, and not for one emerald less. Sometimes I give a fine thing that grows warm when carried, but who would throw away a fine thing? Sometimes I am a nanny, and lead the village children home, where the fire is always burning high.
message.grandwitch.broom.broke: The broom has fallen to bits!
message.grandwitch.feed.eat: <%s> Oh, thank you, what a good child...
message.grandwitch.feed.suspect: <%s> This cake... it smells wrong! Do you mean to harm me?
message.grandwitch.witch_mouse: The Grand Witch has shrunk to a mouse! Quick, now! She is shining.
message.grandwitch.witch_back: The Grand Witch is herself again!
message.grandwitch.broom.mouse: A mouse cannot get up on a broom
item.grandwitch.plague_virus.tip: Taken from wild mice (a player has to kill them) and from the witch. Add it to an awkward potion in a brewing stand for the potion of the mouse; gunpowder makes it splash, dragon's breath lingering, and a lingering one with arrows makes tipped arrows.
